title: Role-Based Access Control
definition: RBAC: An authorization strategy where permissions are assigned to specific roles (Admin, Editor, Viewer), and users are granted those roles.
simpleExplanation: A standard user logs in and sees 'View Article'. An Admin logs in and sees 'View Article' AND 'Delete Article'. The system checks their 'role' before rendering UI elements or allowing API requests.
realWorldExample: A SaaS application with 'Free Tier' and 'Pro Tier' users. Pro users are authorized to access the `/advanced-analytics` route, while Free users are blocked.

basic: If Authentication answers 'Are you logged in?', what does Authorization answer?
intermediate: Why is it critical to check user roles on the Server/API, rather than just hiding the 'Delete' button in the React UI?

answers.question: Why check on server?
answers.answer: Because the client is in the hands of the enemy. A malicious user can easily open Chrome DevTools, make a hidden 'Delete' button visible, and click it. The server API must verify their role before actually deleting the data.
